messages:
Nadia: Quick sync: I'm leaning toward making the model manifest the canonical place for precision "opinions" (supported bitwidths, safety envelope, quick smoke anchors). Pros/cons?
Omar: I like a single source of truth. Concern: customers need per-tenant tuning and platform teams need to be able to enforce SLAs.
Sophie: Proposal: manifest fields = precision_candidates, safety_budget (float), quality_anchor_hash, latency_delta_estimate, cost_delta_estimate, allowed_overrides, deprecation_window_days, fallback_policy_id, manifest_version, signature.
Theo: Important: include "regen_policy" enum: {NONE, SOFT_APPEND, REGENERATE_OPT_IN, FORCE_REGENERATE} so runtime and clients can agree on behavior if we fallback mid-stream.
Nadia: Streaming clients are fragile. For FORCE_REGENERATE we need client SDK support. Default for hosted API should be SOFT_APPEND and only allow REGENERATE_OPT_IN. Note these are part of the manifest contract.
Omar: For per-tenant overrides: runtime can accept overrides but must do validation checkpoints: pre-accept (is override in allowed_overrides?), approx_degradation_check (estimation vs safety_budget), and post-exec telemetry check (did degscore drift > budget?). If post-exec fails, mark override as revoked for that tenant and trigger remediation.
Sophie: We should bake a small quality_anchor (e.g., 32-token example or 8-dim digest) that can be checked cheaply during canaries and post-deploy sampling. Manifest stores quality_anchor_hash and where to fetch the artifact.
Theo: Signing + versioning for Dedicated/Private is mandatory. Add admin-ack timestamp and acceptance token for private installs. Also need a migration policy if safety_budget tightens mid-flight: deprecation_window_days and staged enforcement.
Nadia: UX: when customers request override we should return structured error code with explainers: OVERRIDE_REJECTED_OUTSIDE_BOUNDS, OVERRIDE_VIOLATES_DEGR_BUDGET, OVERRIDE_PENDING_REMEDIATION. Keep messages concise and machine-parseable.
Omar: Observability: emit canary report metrics per manifest + per-precision: sample_loss_delta, latency_delta, token_cost_delta, regen_rate, early_fallback_rate. Use these for automated rollback rules.
Sophie: Edgecase: per-layer or headwise exceptions (some attention heads are sensitive) 12 allow manifest to include per-namespace exceptions: e.g., disallow 4bit for attention_kv on certain shapes. That is complex but allows safer lowbit paths.
Theo: Implementation plan sketch: 1) RFC with manifest schema + regen_policy enum; 2) runtime override validation checkpoints and error codes; 3) manifest signing + admin acceptance API; 4) canary smoke tests using quality_anchor; 5) console UX to show latency/cost/quality deltas and whether an override is allowed.
Nadia: Action items: Nadia  draft RFC and include sample canary dashboard. Omar  write override validation spec and error codes. Sophie  define quality_anchor format and minimal artifact size. Theo  draft signing/migration admin flow for Dedicated/Private. I'll collect and post a short RFC link tomorrow.
manifest-bot: RFC created: /rfc/manifest-precision-orchestration-v1 12 reviewers: Nadia, Omar, Sophie, Theo
